text: A collateral-insurance claim is a guarantee_claim row whose claim_type is the member COLLATERAL_INSURANCE of LOV-CLAIM-TYPE, whose claimed_amount is the appraised value the collateral read returns, and whose claim_deadline is the date the filing officer records for the insurer's claim window. No deadline basis, claimed-amount basis or retention rule is stated for this claim type, so the branch asserts none and carries every value as data with its version; the required set of the element stays as TSD S3 T3.1 fixes it, and a missing deadline or amount is refused with MSG-GEN-001 rather than supplied by a default.
why: The row requires claim_deadline and claimed_amount, the feature is silent on both for a collateral-insurance claim, and the 32 GUA rows carry no collateral-insurance row that could supply them.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-020 AC1 and Data table; FSD S3 A2.8.2 and A2.8.3.1 to A2.8.3.2; TSD S3 T3.1, T3.2, T5.1; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DEV-06, R-DEV-09, R-LIT-79; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-GUA-08; context pack S3 ownership rows; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-05 and §R9
confirm: Business owner of module S3 with the insurer claim owner at the wave 3 contract freeze
impact: If a source later fixes a deadline rule or a claimed-amount basis, only the rule read and the validation of the two elements change; the row, the branch and the record are unchanged

text: The re-appraisal is a request on the case signal and not a call: this service reports the filed claim and the re-appraisal request to the parent CaseWorkflow of rwb-case, which applies the case state, and the route stage orders the appraisal under FEAT-VAL-01 in rwb-valuation. No rwb-valuation operation, no appraisal order and no SVAF exchange is declared by this service, because Architecture v5 slide 13 gives S3 no REST edge to S1, so the request adds no contract and no class C dependency; the plan's C, I and X rows stay empty and the branch builds on Day 1 without the route service.
why: The legacy story depends on FEAT-VAL-01, the feature names SVAF, and no source publishes a re-appraisal operation or an S3-to-S1 edge, so the trigger has to travel the route the connection matrix already gives.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-020 AC1, Depends on FEAT-VAL-01; FSD S3 A2.8.2 integration points Workbench and SVAF; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 FEAT-GUA-08 and FEAT-VAL-01; FSD S8 A2.16.1 to A2.16.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-79; context pack S3 connection matrix row S3 and slide 13; Template and Rules §R5.4 classes C and I

text: The collateral and appraisal facts are read through rwb-source-data's contract and not through a v_ace_* grant in rwb_guarantee: the service holds no grant on the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views, and the operation name, its request and answer fields, the field identifiers of v_ace_collateral, v_ace_collateral_detail and v_ace_valuation, the key that matches them to the case and the freshness rule are not published. The client is therefore built on Day 1 against the documented use and a fake, one hop and 2 s timeout, and the absence adds no class C row because DP-05 adds no dependency.
why: Slide 8 reserves the ACE views to rwb-source-data, the legacy story reads three of them on its own connection, and no source publishes the contract that replaces them.

text: The GUARANTEE rule set holds no collateral-insurance row, so the branch applies the two rows FSD S3 A2.8.3.1 states - VR-S3-008-1 and BR-S3-008 - with the rule package in force, honours the person-approval condition of R-DEV-06 (a person approves an insurance claim), and records the outcome as R-DEV-09 does for X7. No threshold, window, deadline, share or state is taken from a GUA row and none is invented, and the X7 deviation of FEAT-DVF-07 stays with rwb-deviation.
why: The feature states two rows, the workbook's 32 GUA rows name none of them for a collateral-insurance claim, and R-DEV-06 is the only row that governs who may file.

text: The claim row states are the five members of LOV-CLAIM-STATUS and the case and deviation states named by R-DEV-06, R-DEV-09 and R-LIT-79 belong to rwb-deviation and rwb-case; no source maps the two vocabularies, so the branch writes the row state PREPARING and FILED and reports the case outcome without a state name of its own. The X7 collateral event reaches this service on the case signal from rwb-case and never on a topic of this service, because the ownership rows give S3 no event and no subscription to S8.
why: The two vocabularies exist side by side in the sources and the stage must move the record and the case in one act without inventing a map.

why: The overlay for D-RCV-60 records a missing approval or status as an assumption and continues at Draft rather than stopping the run.

text: The contract publishes the collateral and appraisal elements as placeholders in major version 1: collateralNo, collateralType, collateralValue, appraisalNo, appraisedValue and appraisalDate, all optional with no default, named in camelCase after the legacy columns collateral_no, collateral_type, collateral_value, appraisal_no, appraised_value and appraisal_date of the Data table of the key. They carry no field identifier and create no column of guarantee_claim, the answer returns exactly the elements it was given, and the names are replaced by the published identifiers without a breaking change when the data owner allocates them.
why: The branch needs the collateral and the appraisal on the claim, the row has eight fields and none of them holds either, and no field identifier is published for them.
